name: Ecne

attributes.attribute: the Irish god of wisdom, son of three gods of craft
a magic fish whose flesh imparts wisdom
the hidden well that keeps the wisdom fish

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Ecne is an Irish deity of wisdom. His name means wisdom. Three gods of craft and knowledge are his fathers. That birth links wisdom to the body. He also holds a bond to water. A person gains wisdom by eating a magic salmon. The fish lives in a hidden well called Segais. Wisdom is earned by effort, not given as grace. Yet the effort is more Otherworldly than plain work. This wisdom also reaches into the arts.

okr.objective: Present the Irish god of wisdom as a figure won by effort through the body, water, and the arts.
key_results: His name means wisdom and three gods of craft are his fathers.
A person gains wisdom by eating a magic salmon from a hidden well.
Wisdom is earned by effort, not given like grace.
That wisdom also feeds the arts.
